dataset: Correlation study - measured, specified and missing

method.measured: Pearson rho with Fisher-z 95% interval, computed on the 32-club verified aggregates
method.specified: analytic rho from the model's error structure (iid normal team points, sigma = declared prior)
method.missing: left blank on purpose; needs play-by-play (flag F-16)

measured.reads: How much of 'good offence' is really 'good defence'. A strongly negative value would mean quality teams also allow fewer points, so spread and total legs would inherit that coupling.
measured.implication_for_parlays: Near zero means the static model does not itself create extra dependence between a side and a total; any real dependence must come from game flow.

measured.pair: net points per game vs win percentage
measured.reads: Whether the standings are internally coherent as a rating.
measured.implication_for_parlays: Validation that PF/PA is a usable strength signal at all; a weak value would condemn the whole v0 model.

measured.pair: games played vs net points per game
measured.reads: Does a short season (bye taken) line up with quality?
measured.implication_for_parlays: If games-played correlated with strength, per-game rates would carry a schedule-size artefact.

measured.pair: club projected absences (Out+Doubtful) vs net points per game
measured.reads: Is availability injury-driven, quality-driven or noise? This is the single most important check before letting injury data move a line: a strong negative value means the two signals overlap and an additive injury penalty double-counts weakness.
measured.implication_for_parlays: Sets the ceiling on how much an availability adjustment should be trusted.

measured.pair: club projected absences vs points per game
measured.reads: Same test on the offence side only.
measured.implication_for_parlays: If offence-side absences track scoring, part of the injury 'signal' is already inside PPG.

measured.pair: club projected absences vs points allowed per game
measured.reads: Same test on the defence side only.
measured.implication_for_parlays: If defensive absences track points allowed, an adjustment on OUT defensive players double-counts.

measured.pair: offence absences vs defence absences, same club
measured.reads: Do clubs lose hitters on both sides at once (poor depth, poor medical staff, small roster)?
measured.implication_for_parlays: High value means a 'both sides thin' bucket exists, which is a total-market signal, not a spread one.

leg_pairs.pair: Home spread + away spread, same game
leg_pairs.how: identical statistic, opposite sign - one leg wins exactly when the other loses
margin = H-A and total = H+A are orthogonal when both teams carry the same variance; under the model's iid normal errors the correlation is exactly zero
leg_pairs.needs_data: the zero result depends on equal variances and on ignoring game flow; a trailing team passing more makes over + dog-spread positively dependent in reality - that term needs play-by-play

leg_pairs.pair: Team A spread + Team A team total
Team A spread + Team B spread (same game)
Two legs from two different games
leg_pairs.how: no shared term in a static model; cross-game dependence in practice is small and not modelled

leg_pairs.pair: Player prop + that player's team spread
leg_pairs.how: not computable here - requires snap-weighted usage and game-state response

leg_pairs.pair: Two props on the same player (e.g. pass yards + completions)
leg_pairs.how: not computable here - requires the joint distribution of one player's game

leg_pairs.pair: Same-player props on the same side of a high-total game
leg_pairs.how: not computable here - the coupling is exactly the game-flow term

parlay_pricing_rule: A parlay is priced from the JOINT probability, never from the product of legs. For k legs with the correlation matrix R above, P(all win) is evaluated with the bivariate/multivariate normal integral using R; where an entry of R is blank the parlay is not priced at all (gate G6 returns HOLD).

bvn_examples.joint: 0 (impossible for both sides of one game to win)
